sections.skill: Write short procedures and block time for admin

questions.prompt: What is a procedure in a small business?

choices.text: A legal filing that registers the business
Written steps for a task that repeats
A one-time speech the owner gives on opening day
A medical operation for the business owner

questions.correct_answer: Written steps for a task that repeats
questions.intro: A PROCEDURE (or checklist) writes down the steps for a task that repeats, such as opening the shop, packing an order, or closing out the day. Written steps reduce mistakes, make work faster, and let a helper do the task the same way. Keep each checklist short, in order, and updated when something changes. A simple SCHEDULE blocks time for paid work, for admin (invoices, email, bookkeeping) and for rest, so important tasks are not always pushed to "later."

questions.prompt: A business checklist is like what?
questions.intro: A recipe card lists ingredients and steps in order, so anyone in the family can make the dish the same way. If a step changes, like a new oven temperature, you update the card. A business checklist is a recipe card for a work task: short, in order, and kept up to date. A weekly schedule is like a meal plan: it decides when each thing gets done.
